item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ long screed
- Hide text

So, I've refrained generally from commenting on this series. This is in no way shape or form my thing stylistically. But this piece almost works as a standalone article, and it's got some issues that I feel are applicable to a lot of work on the wiki. So allow me to climb onto a soap box for a minute.

Unlike a lot of people commenting here, I don't feel length works against this piece. Its strength is actually in the storytelling, and it does tell a fairly disturbing story that I find compelling, despite my distaste for this series, Wondertainment and GOI fuckery in general. It veers into cliched crazy guy devices at times and is a little too coherent for someone as apparently psychotic as Redd, but these are forgivable and don't ultimately derail what you're going for.

What does derail this piece, though, is this:

seriously dude though for real what the fuuuuuuck.

I MADE YOU TOTES FUCKIN' ANGRY AND SHIT
and i was like grrr yeah i'm a bit angry and stuff hehe
[the rest of that entire section]

and everyone just SPAZZED THE FUCK OUT

I KNOW RIGHT

YEAH I KNOW SERIOUSLY

So Mr. Redd is a seriously misguided attempt by a mad genius to be a living instrument to amuse/educate children. And he's been given insanity-inducing amounts of anger and rage that don't have any basis in anything except they've been put there to make him a tool. He's built and dehumanized for a twisted, loathesome purpose and he's still cognizant enough to realize it. That's fucked up on a bunch of different levels, and it's very good material for writing something.

So you've got me. Despite my prejudices, you've got me and I'm interested. And then, this profoundly damaged individual, who you're working so very hard to make both terrifying and sympathetic, who as a person is probably completely unrelatable to anyone with even a shred of sanity, talks like a dude posting stuff in Site 19. So instead of achieving what you've set out to do, which is (despite your affectations) to make a serious and moving piece, you've set me up to roll my eyes so hard that they're going to fall out of my head.

I feel cheated.

I mean, you're telling me that Mr. Redd, a fucking transdimensional man-clone implanted with inhuman rage AND a functioning soul, who basically is thrown into a world that doesn't want him and that he will never have any hope of understanding, he's going to lace his dialogue with "totes angry", call people "dude", and generally be up on current internet-speak? Fuck that. That's lazy writing.

This is a problem that a LOT of people have. Maybe I should go easier on you for that, but it annoys me that something that comes so close to achieving something of genuine value gets ruined by the author not wanting to imagine what it would be like for someone who's not them to talk.

I would really, really like to see people think about this more when they write characters. If we're going to be seeing daily installments of various stories and narratives populating the site, then we as a community need to work a lot harder on stretching our imaginations to include the experiences of people who aren't IRC-dwelling internet fiction writers. And dialogue is where that shows up most egregiously.

I'm not asking for painstakingly-researched dialogue that's informed by observed speech patterns in 18th-century immigrants to Bolivia or accurate references to common sayings among the Romanian Diaspora in London. But I would really, really appreciate it if people would read over their stuff, and think to themselves "hey, maybe this guy wouldn't say stuff like 'I KNOW RIGHT' or 'I'M TOTES ANGRY', since he's not a twentysomething forum-dweller".

This wouldn't bother me so much if it wasn't sinking articles that I would otherwise have enjoyed. Anyway, standard "Kalinin represents a minority opinion so no one should butcher their article if it's successful, but I'm just saying" disclaimer here. I will reevaluate my vote pending any future changes.
